comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Expense Increase and AI Headcount
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's research and development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher employee-related costs resulting from an increase in headcount to support the company's AI strategy.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD attribute their increases in Research & Development (R&D) expenses for fiscal year 2024 primarily to employee-related costs driven by headcount growth. NVDA explicitly links R&D expense increases to 'compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, reflecting employee growth' (nvda_2024_7_P061_S001). Similarly, AMD states its R&D expense increase was 'primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy' (amd_2024_7_P045_S002), confirming a shared driver of personnel expansion in R&D functions.

sentences.text: The increase in research and development expenses and sales, general and administrative expenses for fiscal year 2024 was primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, reflecting employee growth and compensation increases.
The increase was primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.

comparisons.peer_summary: Marketing, general and administrative expenses were $2.8 billion in 2024, an increase of $431 million or 18% from $2.4 billion in 2023, primarily due to increased go-to-market activities supporting revenue growth.
comparisons.comparison: While NVDA groups Sales, General, and Administrative (SG&A) expenses together with R&D to explain the overall operating expense increase driven by compensation (nvda_2024_7_P061_S001), AMD separately discloses that its Marketing, General, and Administrative (MG&A) expenses also increased in 2024. However, the drivers differ: AMD attributes its MG&A increase primarily to 'go-to-market activities to support our revenue growth' (amd_2024_7_P046_S002), whereas NVDA highlights compensation and benefits for its combined operating expenses.

sentences.text: The increase in research and development expenses and sales, general and administrative expenses for fiscal year 2024 was primarily driven by compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, reflecting employee growth and compensation increases.
The increase was primarily due to an increase in go-to-market activities to support our revenue growth.
